text:
I’ve been a Checkatrade member for a while, and to be fair, it used to generate good-quality work. Unfortunately, over the last year or so, the quality of the leads has dropped dramatically.

My most recent enquiries have been a complete waste of time. Customers either don’t respond to calls or messages, the only one recently that did respond told me they hadn’t even booked me when I turned up. As a paying member, that’s simply not good enough.

What frustrates me most is that instead of improving the quality of the leads, Checkatrade seems to be finding more and more ways to charge its members.

First there’s the standard membership fee, where the quality of enquiries has become increasingly poor. Then you’re encouraged to pay extra to promote your business for better visibility, with very little indication of what additional exposure you’ll actually receive.

Next came Express Jobs. Checkatrade takes payment from the customer and then offers the work out to tradespeople at rates that often don’t reflect the time or responsibility involved. For example, I recently saw a three-bedroom EICR paying just £131.50. A proper EICR can easily take 3–5 hours, plus travel, certification and overheads. That’s simply not a sustainable rate for many professional electricians.

Now there’s another feature called “Opportunities”, where members have to buy credits just to express interest in other leads they have on offer , while up to three other tradespeople can do exactly the same. You can pay  more for the chance to quote and still never hear anything back.

From my perspective, the focus seems to have shifted away from providing quality work for tradespeople and towards creating more ways for members to spend money and check a trade to make more money .

It’s a real shame because Checkatrade once worked well for my business. Sadly, I won’t be renewing when my contract ends, and I hope other tradespeople carefully consider whether it still offers value before signing up.

text:
Over four years with Checkatrade – lead quality and support have declined
I have been a Checkatrade member for over four years, since June 2022. Near the beginning, there was a period when the number and quality of enquiries dropped, and many leads appeared questionable or contained very little useful information. After speaking with the Checkatrade team, the situation improved and I started receiving genuine work again.
Unfortunately, the same problem has now returned. Since April, I have secured only a few genuine, relatively small jobs through Checkatrade. I still receive enquiries, but many appear to have been written very quickly and contain almost no useful information about the work required. Some seem questionable, and customers often never respond after I contact them.
I always try to respond quickly, usually within an hour of receiving an enquiry, but in many cases I hear nothing back at all. When paying £117 per month, which is £1,404 per year, I would expect better-quality leads and a more reasonable return for the cost.
We always make every effort to provide a high standard of workmanship and a reliable, professional service. Our customers have consistently been pleased with the quality of our work, and all the reviews on our Checkatrade profile are positive. These genuine reviews not only help build our own business reputation, but also contribute to Checkatrade’s reputation and give customers confidence in the platform.
This makes it even more disappointing that, despite paying a substantial monthly fee and maintaining an excellent review record, we now receive so few genuine and worthwhile opportunities.
I also emailed Checkatrade to explain the problem, but I did not receive a response. That is particularly disappointing considering that I have been a paying member for more than four years.
A friend recently asked me whether joining Checkatrade was worthwhile. I told him honestly about my recent experience, and he decided not to join. I also know another tradesperson working in London who initially received work through Checkatrade but now keeps his membership mainly because of the good customer reviews already attached to his profile.
Would I currently recommend becoming a Checkatrade member? Unfortunately, no. Unless the quality of enquiries and customer support improve significantly, I do not believe it will be worthwhile renewing my contract when the current term ends.
Checkatrade used to work well for my business, which makes the recent decline even more disappointing. I hope they properly investigate the quality of the enquiries being submitted, respond to long-standing members when concerns are raised, and improve the overall value of the service.

I recently moved home and, based on the trust I placed in Checkatrade, used two tradespeople sourced through your platform. Unfortunately, both experiences have resulted in property damage, considerable stress, and, so far, little confidence that these matters are being addressed appropriately.

1. Removals Company

The removals company I engaged provided what I can only describe as an unprofessional service. During the move they damaged several of my possessions, including:

* Breaking my TV cabinet.
* Scraping and denting my Bosch fridge freezer, which was in pristine condition prior to the move.

When I first raised these issues, the company denied responsibility. They subsequently accepted that the damage had occurred and agreed to put matters right. However, despite those assurances, they have now stopped responding to my emails and I have been left with damaged property and no resolution.

2. TV Removal and Wall Mounting

The second incident is significantly more serious.

I instructed a trader listed on Checkatrade, to professionally remove my 65-inch LG G5 OLED television from the wall at my previous property, transport it to my new home, and reinstall it.

This television was less than one year old, had cost approximately £2,900, and was in immaculate, unmarked condition before carried out the work.

Following installation at my new property, I discovered visible damage to the television’s frame. The damage was not present before the move. The television had been handled solely by the tradesman during the removal, transportation and reinstallation process.

Although the television appears to function, it has suffered cosmetic damage to what was previously a pristine, premium television. I have retained evidence of its condition and the damage.

What has caused me additional concern is the tradesman conduct after the incident. The business represented that it had public liability insurance, yet when I requested details to enable me to pursue a claim, there was reluctance to provide the insurer’s information. I also became aware that he does not appear to be registered at Companies House despite presenting itself in a way that suggested it was an established business.

As a consumer, I relied on the fact that this trader was listed on Checkatrade as an indication that appropriate checks had been carried out and that I would be dealing with a reputable and accountable business.

My Complaint Regarding Checkatrade

I have already submitted a complaint through your complaints procedure. To date, I have received no meaningful update or response.

I find this extremely disappointing given that both traders were sourced directly through your platform. I chose Checkatrade because of its reputation and the confidence it gives consumers when selecting tradespeople. In this instance, that confidence has been seriously undermined.

I would appreciate an urgent response addressing the following:

* Confirmation that my complaints have been received and are being investigated.
* An update on the action being taken regarding both traders.
* Whether either incident may be eligible under the Checkatrade Guarantee or any other customer protection available through Checkatrade.
* Confirmation of the checks that were undertaken before the tradesmen were permitted to advertise on your platform.
* A clear timescale for your investigation and response.

I hope these matters can be resolved promptly. If I do not receive a satisfactory response within a reasonable timeframe, I will have little option but to consider escalating my concerns to the relevant consumer protection bodies and, where appropriate, pursuing recovery of my losses directly through the appropriate legal channels.

I look forward to hearing from you as a matter of urgency

I remain willing to resolve the matter reasonably and in writing, but I cannot recommend the service based on our experience.

text:
Avoid if you're looking for genuine commercial leads

We were contacted by Checkatrade and sold their advertising service by Shivani Shashidar. During the sales process, we made it very clear that our business provides commercial joinery, electrical and fit-out services, and that we do not operate in the domestic market. We specifically stated that we only wanted commercial leads.

We were assured this would not be a problem and that the platform could provide suitable commercial enquiries. Based on those assurances, we proceeded with the vetting process and signed up.

Almost immediately, we started receiving hundreds of enquiries for domestic jobs that were completely irrelevant to our business. When we logged into the system, we discovered that Checkatrade had set up two advertising campaigns on our behalf that we had neither authorised nor approved. We turned these campaigns off, only to find them switched back on later, resulting in even more unsuitable enquiries.

Checkatrade subsequently admitted that they had created and activated these campaigns themselves. They also advertised the wrong address, using my home address, and the advertisements were not branded as we had expected. We were told various changes could be made only after the account had already gone live and the vetting process had been completed.

Despite repeatedly explaining that the service was not as sold to us and was wholly unsuitable for our business, we have continued to receive demands for over £3,500 in fees. We have made numerous complaints and have repeatedly been told an investigation is required, even though Checkatrade has acknowledged that the campaigns were created and activated by them, not by us.

Had we been told from the outset that the platform could not effectively differentiate between commercial and domestic opportunities, we would never have signed up. In our experience, the service simply does not work for commercial businesses like ours.

Furthermore, the much-publicised vetting process does not appear to assess the quality of workmanship or suitability of contractors in the way many consumers may expect.

Based on our experience, we would not recommend Checkatrade to commercial contractors seeking relevant leads, and we would encourage both tradespeople and customers to carry out their own due diligence before signing up or relying on the platform.

Thank you for your reply to my previous review.

I appreciate your response, but simply asking me to call your support team does not address the issues I have raised.

Around two months ago, Checkatrade charged me approximately double for a product that I had never requested. Following my complaint, I received an apology acknowledging that this charge should not have been applied.

In my view, this fundamentally changed the agreement between us. I had agreed to pay for one service, not for additional products or charges that I had never authorised. As a result, I lost confidence in the billing process and cancelled the Direct Debit until the matter could be resolved.

At that point, I specifically requested a call with a manager so that I could make the following month's payment once the billing error had been corrected. That call never happened.

This is exactly why I believe Trustpilot should distinguish between reviews of tradespeople and reviews of Checkatrade as a business. Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited subscribed to Checkatrade based on the representations made regarding the enquiries provided to tradespeople through the platform.

During the subscription period, Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited raised concerns regarding a number of enquiries received through the service. These concerns related to overlapping contact details and enquiries which, in the view of Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited, warranted further investigation.

In correspondence, Checkatrade explained that some situations could arise through homeowner error and indicated that duplicate submissions could not always be completely prevented. However, Checkatrade’s later court Defence stated that its investigation had identified no duplicate, non-genuine or spam leads. Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited considered this difficult to reconcile with the earlier correspondence, and it formed part of the concerns raised throughout the dispute.

Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited subsequently requested cancellation of the subscription. Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited understood from Checkatrade’s correspondence that cancellation was to be dealt with by telephone. Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited requested that communications be conducted in writing by email so that a clear and verifiable record could be maintained.

When the matter was not resolved, Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited issued a Letter Before Action and subsequently commenced County Court proceedings.

Following the commencement of proceedings, Checkatrade issued a credit memo. The matter later proceeded to a Dispute Resolution Hearing before the County Court.

At the hearing, Checkatrade confirmed to the court that the agreement/subscription had been cancelled, that no further payments were due from Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited, and that any sums allegedly due had been written off. The court order records Checkatrade’s confirmation that the agreement/subscription had been cancelled, that no further payments were due from Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited, and that any sums allegedly due had been written off. The claim was dismissed and no order as to costs was made.

The purpose of the proceedings was not primarily to recover money, but to obtain certainty that the subscription had been brought to an end and that no future debt recovery action would be pursued.

Based on this experience, tradespeople should carefully review contractual terms, maintain detailed written records, and obtain important information and confirmations in writing wherever possible. Where agreements are discussed by telephone, it may be prudent to request written confirmation of the key terms before accepting or proceeding with any agreement.

This review reflects the experience of Dare’s Cleaning Services Limited and the outcome recorded in the County Court order.

The tradesman was punctual and opened  the door quickly, though the preceded in taking a long time to determine the problem.

Amazing, or so we thought. 

Two days later messaged the tradesman asking if he had the part, to which the response was “it was meant to arrive today, will keep you informed”.

That was the last time they responded and following multiple calls, messages etc over a period of time we reached out to Checkatrade.

The same evidence was then issued to the “seperate” guarantee team who turned the claim down within 24hours without any rationale.

Requesting the rationale, they have provided me with an account from the tradesman, no evidence just an account.

Since this I have videos from my Ring Doorbell where they are on the phone to another locksmith asking for advice and saying on multiple occasions they need more training.

I would steer clear of using Checkatrade, suggest recommendations elsewhere as if the worst happens they will accept an account over whatever you might have.

Now this is only over c.£100 which seems petty when reading another’s similar review, and for me it’s not the money it’s the deceitfulness of an individual and Checkatrades lack of care for the consumers.

text:
I chose a tradesperson through Checkatrade partly because of the reassurance provided by the Checkatrade Guarantee.

Unfortunately, my experience has left me extremely disappointed.

I hired a painter and decorator through Checkatrade to carry out extensive works at my property, including wallpaper removal, wall preparation, lining paper installation and painting throughout multiple rooms. The total amount paid was £2,650.

After the work was completed, I identified numerous issues with the workmanship, including poor wall preparation, visible defects through the lining paper, uneven finishes and a generally substandard decorating finish across multiple areas of the property. I provided extensive photographic evidence to Checkatrade and raised concerns with the tradesperson.

Throughout the complaint process, I dealt with multiple different representatives and repeatedly had to provide the same information and explanations. At various stages, I was asked again for information that had already been submitted.

The tradesperson initially suggested additional payments were owed, despite previously acknowledging receipt of the agreed contract amount. When the dispute remained unresolved, I applied under the Checkatrade Guarantee expecting an independent and thorough review of the workmanship issues.

Despite providing photographs, correspondence, payment evidence and details of the agreed works, my claim was ultimately rejected. The decision letter did not clearly explain which specific evidence had been assessed, what standard had been applied, or why the defects shown in the photographs were considered insufficient.

The outcome left me with the impression that the Guarantee offers far less practical protection than consumers may expect when choosing a Checkatrade member.

My concern is not simply that my claim was unsuccessful. It is that the process lacked transparency, there was no independent inspection of the work, and significant evidence appeared to have been disregarded.

Consumers should carefully review the terms and conditions of the Guarantee and understand exactly what evidence may be required before relying on it as a source of protection.

Based on my experience, I would not place significant reliance on the Checkatrade Guarantee when choosing a tradesperson.

Rating: ★☆☆☆☆

This review reflects my personal experience with Checkatrade’s complaints and guarantee process.

I would strongly advise potential customers to consider how they might be treated if something goes wrong.

text:
The website is easy to navigate and it's relatively easy to find businesses for what you might need doing.  Some of whom might respond to your offer of work.

There is some valuable information about the status of the businesses. 

The problem is that in our experience the ratings are not necessarily representative of real world work competence nor quality. 

Even in person they might seem good and refer to good ratings, in practice they have not been. 

The best option (should be made compulsory for all businesses) in the future for us is to choose only those businesses where payment is made through checkatrade who will try to arbitrate if work is below standard. Without this they have no ability for the business to make things right or compensate as we have discovered so alternative legal routes have had to be tried. 

Always make payments through credit card as it is possible to dispute if work is below par. Always have a full written quote with no ambiguities. Be careful of businesses without fixed costs. Read the business contract/quote as some give the businesses ability to add costs and you will not be able to dispute them. 

Finally nice does not necessarily mean good, and 5 stars doesn't necessarily mean competent/quality. And this if you're unlucky is a problem.

text:
I've used Checkatrade before and had good experiences (hence, the 2 stars instead of 1), so I'm leaving this review only to warn others that a "Verified Tradesperson" profile does not guarantee that someone is genuine.

I needed an urgent repair done within 48 hours, and this person was the only one who said he could do it in time. He asked for a deposit for materials, which I reluctantly paid because his profile showed "Address Checked" and "Identity Checked," and he had a few reviews and photos of previous work. He never showed up, stopped responding to calls and messages, and the profile was then cancelled. text:
I am 62 days into my second year's subscription. I pay for the basic lead service for one trade and have activated a geographical catchment area with a population exceeding 250,000 people.

My Checkatrade campaign homepage suggests I should have received between 13-19 leads thus far. I have received 3. One lead, the contact details dont work, the next is budgeting only and the last was to repair a dent in a wall, which I didn't even bother responding to. 

By their own standards and compared to the  alternative providers I use, this is really very poor, in fact the worst performer from the 5 different lead provider platforms I currently use.

In addition, leads are capped and provided inline with customer demand and therefore unevenly distributed. The has twofold effects;

If one is expected to receive 120 leads over the course of 12 months, the majority of leads will be received during peak season. One's quota is typically exhausted prior to the end of the 12 month contractual term. I personally only received a couple of leads a month for the final 3-4 months of my first year's subscription.

Secondly; the majority of leads will be received during peak season. You receive the most leads when the market is busy and you likely have a full order book regardless, conversely, you will receive the least when you need them most.

In summary; do not consider this a subscription to 12months of leads, it isn't. You can't rely on a steady lead flow and therefore will need to compliment your subscription with alternative lead sources. When you have reached your quota, this will be a leverage point for Checkatrade to encourage you to subscribe for a larger quota package.

Currently, the service simply isn't fit for purpose and not anywhere near worth the cost. The actual performance vs what is advertised by Checkatrade is bordering misrepresentation. I suspect Checkatrade have pulled back on marketing and lost market share. I seriously regret purchasing another subscription and will do my best to pull out of the contract. 

Do not at this stage subscribe to Checkatrade and get locked into a 12 month contract. Checkatrade's performance is terrible.

text:
For the first few years, Checkatrade was an excellent service. It was good value for money, with customer service that was responsive, that delivered mostly quality leads and was flexible in terms of area selection for where leads should come from.

For the last year, things seem to have changed dramatically, from top-level management all the way down. Customer service is no longer helpful, I receive next to no leads, and the few I do are riddled with marketing spam and timewasters who were never interested in getting a job done in the first place. They also no longer respect my preferences for where leads should come from - I am given leads far outside of my area, that are not worth my time to travel to. 

They now market themselves as an advertising company and do not guarantee any leads. I was contacted earlier last year by them asking me if I wanted to increase my leads in my area of choice for additional payment. Since then, I haven't received a single lead from these areas, indicating to me that they have moved me out of this area behind my back and refuse to admit to this. 

Checkatrade support is extremely unhelpful, insisting that 'no, our algorithm hasn't changed' and insisting that 'we are meeting the terms of your campaign'. They tell me to check the areas I have configured on my profile ad nauseum, even though they haven't changed since the beginning. I have updated my profile, added additional 10/10 customer reviews, and it is still not enough for them. They tell me to ask for reviews; how am I supposed to ask for reviews from leads I'm not getting?

It is unfortunate that I have to follow through on my last words to customer service, and resort to publicly reviewing Checkatrade, as until the last year I have had nothing but good things to say about them. Now, they are unhelpful and are just happy to take my Direct Debit, and even want to start cutting into my leads through services like Checkatrade Pay and Checkatrade Express.
